clue.text: With which we shall have a measure of heat shown on a page?

definitions.text: With which we shall have a measure of heat shown on a page?

parts.note: taken as written
a therm is a unit of heat energy

explanation.surface: A question about the device that will let us see some temperature reading printed on a page.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a weather map is exactly where we see temperatures printed on a page.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather maps in newspapers show forecast temperatures, so one is the thing on which a heat reading appears in print.

clue.text: What could be shot in Ambridge?

definitions.text: What could be shot in Ambridge?

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or broken, so the letters of the place name are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A question about what gets shot in the village of Ambridge, setting of the long-running BBC radio farming soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as firing a gun, which also gives the definition: a pheasant could well be shot in a rural village like Ambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants, grouse and partridges are birds hunted for sport, the typical quarry of a country shoot.

clue.text: A heavenly body appearing in religious texts

parts.note: Vesta is one of the largest asteroids in the solar system

explanation.surface: A star or planet turns up in scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' is only a link here, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the collection of sacred scriptures of Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: Shock when publicity ploy falls short

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a stunt is something done to attract attention

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked when a promotional gimmick fails.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or daze them, as a shock does.

clue.text: One has two hands raised

parts.note: it sounds like someone with both hands in the air, but it is a tall building whose clock face, with hour and minute hands, is held up high

explanation.walkthrough: The hands are a clock's, and they are raised because the clock sits high on a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure with a large clock face near the top, such as Big Ben's tower at Westminster.

clue.text: One studying a bit of poetry will talk

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a verse is one section of a poem

explanation.surface: A student of poetry will chat about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to have a conversation, a synonym for chatting.

clue.text: One in a boat — gentleman given cheer standing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Sir is the title or address for a gentleman
rah is a cheer, as in hurrah

explanation.surface: A gentleman on a boat stands up when he is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a boat' points to Jerome K Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat, whose three men are J, George and Harris.
explanation.definitionFit: Harris is one of the three rowing companions in the novel Three Men in a Boat.

clue.text: Bit of a sweat that has adult laid up?

indicators.note: the bed has, or holds, the adult inside it

parts.note: someone laid up is confined to bed
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A sweaty patch on someone who has been ill in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid up' supplies BED, the place where the ill are kept, and 'has' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead of sweat is a single drop of perspiration.

clue.text: Supposed creative force that could make a lad mostly violent, loveless

indicators.note: the remaining letters could make the answer once rearranged
mostly means most of the word but not all, so lad loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O, so loveless means the O is taken away

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: Some driving force could turn a boy into a brute with no love in him.
explanation.walkthrough: A and LA (lad mostly) and VILENT (violent without O) are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergson's philosophical term for a hypothesised vital impulse behind evolution and life.

clue.text: Declaim nothing when meeting judge

parts.note: O looks like the figure zero, nothing
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: An orator holds forth with nothing to say in front of a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak in a pompous, rhetorical manner, as one declaiming does.

clue.text: The excuse when ambassador is let off crime

indicators.note: letting off the ambassador means his letters leave the word

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
a reason is a justification or excuse

explanation.surface: A criminal envoy is released on some pretext.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, so 'ambassador' is HE; letting him off 'The' leaves just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country or sovereign, is among the gravest offences in law.

clue.text: Old fellow left-winger is protected

parts.note: cove is dated slang for a man or chap
a Red is a communist or socialist

explanation.surface: An elderly socialist is kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being covered means being insured or shielded against something, so safeguarded.

clue.text: Show indigenous people, not the first or last, returning

indicators.note: returning means the remaining letters are read backwards
dropping the first and last letters leaves only the middle

parts.note: natives are the people born in a place

explanation.surface: A display of native peoples, minus a couple, comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: NATIVES without N and S gives ATIVE, which read backwards gives the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice stage musical about Eva Perón.

clue.text: Was model with half a thought about advancement made fun of?

parts.note: an artist's model sat for the painter

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes round, or about, the advancement
half means only the first two of the four letters of the thought are kept

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a rise is a promotion or advance

explanation.surface: Was a model, with a half-formed idea about promotion, mocked?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was model' is SAT, as an artist's model sits; the two letters left from 'half' go 'about' the advancement.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise someone is to ridicule them through irony or exaggeration.

clue.text: What's unfortunately upset crew — the alien creature?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: alas expresses regret, much like unfortunately
to man a ship is to crew it
der is German for the, so a foreign 'the'

explanation.surface: A sci-fi line: sadly the crew are disturbed by the alien monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the alien' is not an extraterrestrial but 'the' in a foreign language, here German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A salamander is a lizard-like amphibian, and in legend a creature that lives in fire.

clue.text: Garden site befouled with stains

indicators.note: something befouled is messed up, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A garden plot has been fouled with marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to blacken or defame someone, figuratively sullying their reputation.

clue.text: Old lingo from girl mad women led astray

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so these letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: A crazy girl and some women are misled by an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link; 'astray' tells you to rearrange GIRL MAD WOMEN LED.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval language of northern Germany and the Hanseatic League, spoken from about 1200 to 1600.

clue.text: Honoured member of Pride is meeting journalist

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A gay rights campaigner is feted while meeting a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P on 'Pride' suggests the LGBT event, but it is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: To lionise someone is to treat them as a celebrity, giving them great public acclaim.

clue.text: Support mum during visit

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
in, as in 'in the night', means during
a stay is a visit somewhere

explanation.surface: Backing your mother while she is on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief prop or backbone of something, originally a ship's principal stay rope.

clue.text: A previous entertainer

parts.note: per means a or each, as in 'ten pounds per head'
former means earlier or previous

explanation.surface: An ex-performer, a has-been entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is not the letter but per, as in 'twice a day', 'twice per day'.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is someone who acts, sings or plays for an audience.

clue.text: Country game's moment finishing early

parts.note: RU, rugby union, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: finishing early means the word ends before its last letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'back in a tick'

explanation.surface: A rural match's key moment arrives ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Country is an adjective here, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic describes things of the countryside, such as rural crafts or simple farmhouse furniture.

clue.text: Some parties win ground — as result of this in elections

definitions.text: as result of this in elections

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Political parties gain territory thanks to a shift in voting.
explanation.definitionFit: A swing is the shift in voter support from one party to another between elections, through which seats are won.

clue.text: Songstress is penetrating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Britney ..., the American pop singer
second meaning: pierces, as with a spear

explanation.walkthrough: The singer's surname is also the verb for running something through.
explanation.definitionFit: Britney's surname doubles as the third-person verb meaning stabs or pierces.

clue.text: It's fortified wine that's good for Parisian to drink

indicators.note: the French word takes in the wine, as if drinking it

parts.note: bon is French for good
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman approves of fortified wine to sip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortified wine' looks like port or sherry; the definition is 'It's fortified', and the wine is ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A bastion is a projecting part of a fortification, and figuratively any stronghold.

clue.text: This youngster getting left could make awful noise

indicators.note: the youngster getting L would make the din, so the din is the answer with that letter taken away

parts.note: a babel is a confused din of voices, after the Tower of Babel

explanation.surface: A child who goes off left might make a terrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: adding L to the answer makes BABEL, so the answer is BABEL with L removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is an informal word for a baby or infant.

clue.text: Plant releases indelicate aroma to start with

parts.note: frees means lets go or releases

indicators.note: to start with means the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A flower gives off a coarse smell at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a South African flowering plant of the iris family, prized for its scent.

clue.text: Points one put to newspaper union leader

parts.note: FOC is Father of the Chapel, the shop steward of a print or newspaper union branch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man is presented to the chief of a press union.
explanation.walkthrough: In British newspaper unions a branch is a chapel and its leader the Father of the Chapel, FOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci is the plural of focus, the central points of attention or convergence.

clue.text: Daughter tucked into cheese, as one at reception?

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the cheese

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A girl eats cheese, as a guest might at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' tempts as eating, but it puts D inside BRIE; the reception is a wedding one.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman getting married is the central figure at her wedding reception.

clue.text: Condemn old partner — gosh, a Greek troublemaker!

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
cor is a British exclamation of surprise like gosh
a means one, the Roman numeral I
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Someone denounces their former spouse, exclaiming they are a Greek menace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives I as in one, and COR is a British exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excoriate is to criticise severely, literally to strip the skin off.
